definitions.definition: A state that a system naturally moves toward over time, like a ball rolling to the bottom of a bowl.
definitions.example: A marble always rolls to the lowest point in a bowl; that lowest point is the attractor state.

definitions.definition: A measure of how aligned or ordered something is; in this framework, it's the degree of alignment with God's nature.
definitions.example: A tidy room has high coherence; a messy room has low coherence.

definitions.definition: Getting closer and closer to a value but never quite reaching it, like a line that approaches a curve forever.
definitions.example: A car approaching a stop sign slows down more and more but never exactly stops if you zoom in infinitely.

definitions.definition: A boundary line that separates two different regions of behavior in a system, like the ridge between two valleys.
definitions.example: The ridge of a mountain that divides which side rain flows down to the east or west.

definitions.definition: The law of physics that says things naturally become more disordered over time, like a sandcastle crumbling.
definitions.example: An ice cube melts into a puddle because the Second Law increases disorder.

definitions.definition: A branch of math that studies how things change over time based on rules, like predicting the weather.
definitions.example: A bouncing ball's height over time is a simple dynamical system.

definitions.definition: A map of all possible conditions a system can be in, like a grid of all possible positions and speeds of a car.
definitions.example: For a light switch, the state space has two points: on and off.

definitions.definition: To move toward a single point or value from different starting points, like streams flowing into a lake.
definitions.example: All the runners in a race converge on the finish line.

definitions.definition: The set of starting points that lead to a particular attractor, like all the rain that falls on one side of a mountain and flows to the same river.
definitions.example: Any ball placed on the left side of a ridge will roll to the left valley; that left side is the basin of attraction.

definitions.definition: A picture that shows all possible paths a system can take over time, like a map of all possible routes a car could drive.
definitions.example: A weather map showing wind patterns is a phase portrait of the atmosphere.

definitions.definition: States where a system stops changing, like a pendulum hanging straight down at rest.
definitions.example: A ball at the bottom of a bowl is at a fixed point because it doesn't move.

definitions.definition: A state where a system returns to after being slightly disturbed, like a marble in a bowl that rolls back to the bottom.
definitions.example: A pencil balanced on its tip is unstable; a pencil lying flat is stable equilibrium.

definitions.definition: Growing or shrinking at a rate that speeds up over time, like a virus spreading faster and faster.
definitions.example: Money in a bank account grows exponentially if interest is added each year.

definitions.definition: The boundary around a black hole where nothing, not even light, can escape once crossed.
definitions.example: Once you cross the event horizon, you're pulled inevitably toward the black hole's center.

definitions.definition: A point where gravity becomes infinite, like at the center of a black hole, where our normal physics breaks down.
definitions.example: The center of a black hole is a singularity where matter is crushed to an infinitely small point.

definitions.definition: Relating to the study of heat, energy, and disorder in systems, like how a hot cup of coffee cools down.
definitions.example: The thermodynamic description of a melting ice cube explains why it gets colder.

definitions.definition: The study of the end times or final destiny of the world and humanity, like heaven, hell, and judgment.
definitions.example: Eschatology asks questions about what happens after death and at the end of history.

definitions.definition: Something that stays the same even when other things change, like the total amount of money in a closed system.
definitions.example: In a game of checkers, the number of pieces on the board changes, but the rules are invariant.

definitions.definition: A Greek word meaning 'Word' or 'reason,' used in the Bible to refer to Jesus as the divine order and logic of the universe.
definitions.example: In John 1:1, 'the Word' is Logos, meaning Jesus is the logic behind creation.

definitions.definition: An invisible field that gives particles mass, like a molasses that slows things down; it has a nonzero vacuum, meaning it's never completely empty.
definitions.example: The Higgs field is like a cosmic treacle that makes particles heavy as they move through it.

definitions.definition: In physics, the lowest possible energy state of a field, not necessarily empty space; the Higgs vacuum is not zero.
definitions.example: The vacuum of the Higgs field is like the ground state of a bell that always hums faintly.

definitions.definition: A faint glow of particles that black holes emit, slowly shrinking them over time, even at the event horizon.
definitions.example: Hawking radiation is like a black hole slowly evaporating like a puddle in the sun.

definitions.definition: A theoretical field in this framework representing God's sustaining presence, like a spiritual gravity that holds everything together.
definitions.example: The χ field is like an invisible force that keeps the universe from falling apart completely.

definitions.definition: The lowest possible energy level of a system, like a ball at the bottom of a valley with no extra energy.
definitions.example: An atom's ground state is its most stable, lowest-energy arrangement.

definitions.definition: The belief that everyone will eventually be saved and go to heaven, regardless of their choices.
definitions.example: Universalism says that even people who reject God will end up in heaven.

definitions.definition: The process of becoming more holy and like God over time, not all at once, like slowly cleaning a dirty room.
definitions.example: Progressive sanctification is like a plant growing gradually toward the sun.

definitions.definition: The process of losing order or alignment, like a crowd of people all talking at once becoming a chaotic noise.
definitions.example: A laser beam is coherent; when it scatters, it decoheres into ordinary light.

definitions.definition: In math, the total accumulation of something over time, like the total distance traveled by adding up tiny steps.
definitions.example: The integral of your speed over a trip gives the total distance you traveled.

definitions.definition: The total sum or combination of many smaller parts, like the total score from all the questions on a test.
definitions.example: The aggregate of all your daily choices shapes your character.
